description: Stage 4p dedicated cases. Two outcomes, both recorded honestly. (A) Block-scoped function declarations (`{ function f(){ let x = 1; } f(); }`): the function body `{` gets the block-body catalog at bracket-creation time (predicate: scanning back from the body brace over the return type, the closed parameter list, an optional type-parameter `<...>`, an optional `*` and the name must land on the `function` keyword), so the body's statements are built by the SAME collection channel as every other body (`StatementBuilder.BuildBlock()` -> `HasBuiltBodyStatements` / `CollectBodyStatements`). The declaration itself stays RAW: no declaration-family shell is created, no declaration-family judgement is touched, and the tree is still produced by the legacy `BuildFunctionDeclaration` recursion. (B) Switch case bodies (`switch (x) { case 1: { ... } }`): mounting the catalog on the case body `{` was implemented and then DISABLED by default (`BlockPossibleShape.EnableSwitchCaseBody = false`) because `case <expression>:` makes the build throw `SourceRange is not set` (a `default:` clause works), which sends the whole file through the file-level fallback - not a deliverable state. With the flag off, case bodies stay raw and are built by `BuildCaseBlock`'s legacy recursion: unchanged tree, zero fallback. Every case below therefore asserts: (1) shell-path XML == legacy-path XML byte for byte; (2) AST node-for-node == ts.createSourceFile; (3) two parses give identical XML; (4) no StatementShape/PossibleShape/CatalogGuide leak in XML; (5) no file-level fallback. Takeover counters (`BlockFunctionBodyMountCount` / `SwitchCaseBodyMountCount` / `ControlFlowBodyBraceCount` / `BlockBodyStatementCount`) are asserted by the Stage 4p cases appended to tests/statement-possible/control-flow-body-takeover.mjs and recorded in HANDOFF-s4p.md. The trap group is the safety gate: the switch body `{`, case bodies (flag off), clause-level statements without braces, type literals, object literals and label bodies must NOT mount.

stage4p.stage: Stage 4p (block-scoped function declaration bodies taken over; switch case bodies attempted then safely rolled back)
stage4p.description: Block-scoped function declarations (simple, two statements, return type, generic, nested in a function, inside an if body, inside a case body block) - taken over; switch case bodies (single block, clause-level statements plus a block, default clause, nested control flow inside the case body, nested switch, two case blocks, no trailing semicolon, inside a block, empty case body, mixed statements) - XML/AST gates with the takeover flag off (raw legacy path, zero fallback); arrow/object nesting confirmations; and the trap group (switch without case bodies, type literal with nested object type, object literal without methods, object method, label body, class method).
